# Second review of SEEN-108, attempt 4, from the seen-reviewer subagent

Spawned fresh on opus with the task text of triage record 47 and nothing else, so
it read the code without anchoring on its own earlier findings. It read the
ticket, the journal and the whole 28-file focus set, verified three findings by
reproduction, and returned a verdict of `return` with six findings. It also
checked and declined to raise: no euro sign, no em or en dash outside the
journal, no credential, no browser automation, no euro arithmetic, no live
marketplace call, and the ticket file's `status: doing` with no `## Outcome`,
which is correct at the review stage.

## Findings

- **F1, high, harness/checks.py:66 with sessions.py and gates.py.** The model a
  check records is read from the log named by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, which a
  subagent inherits from the session that spawned it, so a check run by
  seen-implementer records the parent's model rather than the routed one.
  Verified from inside the review subagent: `sessions.current()` returned
  710e96458c5b, the digest every record on this ticket carries for the parent,
  and `sessions.model()` resolved to the parent's transcript, whose last entry
  predated the subagent's turn and contained none of its work. Confirmed here
  independently: of 15,631 entries in this project's logs, after one scout run
  and two reviewer runs, not one carries `isSidechain` true and every model
  entry reads claude-opus-5. With `[routing] shadow` false the gate would refuse
  a slice that ran exactly as routed, naming a remedy the session cannot carry
  out; in shadow `ran_on` reports the parent's model in every row, so SEEN-109's
  window can never see a route being followed.
- **F2, medium, harness/delivery.py:79.** Deleting `rules=thresholds.load(...)`
  from the kpi.measure call leaves every delivered kpi.json with null costs and
  the whole suite green. The repository already holds the guard pattern for this
  function, DeliveredFiguresTest in test_triage.py, added by SEEN-107's third
  review after the same class of defect.
- **F3, medium, harness/kpi.py:110.** No handoff is written after the last
  slice, so the final slice carries no tokens, no cost and no ran_on, and the
  rework rounds fall inside no window at all. Confirmed: this ticket's windows
  are keyed 1, 2 and 3. The docstring claims the keying cured exactly the fault
  it still has for the last slice, and the fixture ends with a handoff after the
  last slice, which the procedure does not produce.
- **F4, medium, harness/agents.py:106.** After a return to solution replaces the
  plan, `routed()` falls back to the strongest tier while the committed copies
  still hold the previous plan's model, so doctor reports drift on a tree nobody
  edited and CI is red on the commit that records the new plan. Reproduced in a
  scratch tree. Same class as F1 of the first review, with a narrower window.
- **F5, low, record 46.** The accepted tdd record quotes "'614.1 is not an
  instance of int'"; check 40 contains "AssertionError: 300.0 is not an instance
  of <class 'int'>" and the string 614.1 appears in no check output in the
  journal. One record after note 42 corrected the same fault and called it the
  one thing the field exists to prevent. Confirmed here.
- **F6, low, harness/agents.py:154.** The detached-head scan skips any journal
  holding a receipt, and `reopen` leaves the receipt in place by design, so a
  reopened ticket falls back to the strongest tier on the pull_request event
  that F1 of the first review was fixed for.
